upstream.name: usdc — dominant
upstream.via: 5 markets: fxUSD/USDC, PYUSD/USDC, RLUSD/USDC, BOLD/USDC, eUSD/USDC

upstream.name: fxusd — material
upstream.via: 2 markets: fxUSD/USDC, reUSD/fxUSD. ⚠️ THE EDGE THAT BROKE 2026-09-22 — fxUSD was cut 5.0 -> 4.5 and usg.md cited 5.0 for nine days, in prose AND in axis-4 arithmetic, and on the public site in four places. Writing this entry is what makes fxusd -> usg DERIVABLE instead of a hand-written assertion on fxUSD's side.

upstream.name: bold — material
upstream.via: BOLD/USDC. ⚠️ BOLD collides with Bold — resolve by address.

upstream.name: reusd-resupply — material
upstream.via: 2 markets: reUSD/scrvUSD, reUSD/fxUSD. ⚠️ RESUPPLY'S reUSD (0x57aB1E00...4Bec, we score 3.5), NOT Re Protocol's (we score 5.0). The weakest named constituent in the book, and the distinction was load-bearing in axis-4 arithmetic on 2026-10-01.

upstream.name: mseth — material
upstream.via: msETH/WETH — the only volatile-collateral market carrying debt

upstream.name: crvusd — minor
upstream.via: USDT/crvUSD. USG is itself a crvUSD-architecture fork, so this is both a constituent and an architectural ancestor.

upstream.name: StakeDAO / Convex-FXN / Curve gauge wrappers — every position is wrapped before it is posted
upstream.note: ⚠️ Collateral is never the raw pair — it is a wrapper receipt, so each position is 3-4 layers deep (USG -> wrapper -> Curve pool -> two stablecoins -> their own backing). Protocol reports exist for curve.md and convex.md; StakeDAO has none.

upstream.name: Market oracle: virtual_price x MIN(coin price)
upstream.note: ⚠️ THE MIN() IS WHY CONSTITUENT EDGES MATTER MORE HERE THAN ELSEWHERE. A pair gives no diversification on the downside: the weaker leg sets the mark, so you take the worse constituent's risk without the benefit of holding two assets.

upstream.name: cbBTC/WBTC and msETH/OUSD — listed markets carrying ZERO debt
upstream.note: Authorised but debt-free at the 2026-08-05 pull, so they carry no weight and are not constituent edges. ⚠️ They are PRE-AUTHORISED CAPACITY: debt can appear with no governance step, at which point cbbtc becomes a live edge.

dependencies.upstream_resolution_rule: ⚠️ EVERY upstream entry MUST carry exactly one resolution: `slug` (one asset we score), `slugs` (a set entry naming several), `terminal: true` + `kind` (never scoreable — oracle, venue, contract, authority, incentive, real-world, protocol), or `unresolved` (scoreable, no report yet = COVERAGE GAP). ⚠️ TERMINAL AND UNRESOLVED ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS and must never be merged: terminal means nothing is missing, unresolved means a report is owed. `address` is REQUIRED wherever the ticker collides in this corpus (DUSD x4, msUSD x3, reUSD x2, USD3 x2, BOLD x2) — a ticker-keyed graph would merge Resupply's reUSD (3.5) with Re Protocol's (5.0).
dependencies.coverage_note: ⚠️ CONSTITUENT-LEVEL by decision 2026-10-01, not market-level. The graph's job is to answer 'this score moved, who must re-read' — which requires the constituent to be a node. The 12-market structure and its headroom distribution stay in usg.md's axis-4 prose, where they already are. ⚠️ All 16 constituents resolve to a report; none is a coverage gap. Debt weights are the 2026-08-05 vintage and are BANDED, not quoted.
dependencies.materiality_basis: Share of DEBT in the markets where this asset is a leg, from the `2026-08-05 14:38 UTC` market pull (total 3,756,460 USG). dominant >=25% · material 5-25% · minor <5%. ⚠️ A BAND, NOT A PERCENTAGE, DELIBERATELY: USG's weights exist in three vintages inside its own report (reUSD/fxUSD 104,463 -> $129,608 -> $230,947) and a decimal rots silently while a band survives drift. ⚠️ AND ASK WHAT THE DENOMINATOR COUNTS: this is share of debt in markets where the asset is A LEG, not share of risk. USG's oracle is virtual_price x MIN(coin price), so only the WORSE leg sets a market's mark — both legs are banded at the market's full weight, which is deliberately conservative and overstates the stronger leg.

downstream_basis.asserted_only_note: None — every asserted edge is reproducible from an upstream array.
downstream_basis.do_not_hand_edit: ⚠️ downstream_tracked is GENERATED. Hand-maintaining both directions is how fxsave came to list fxUSD as BOTH its upstream and its downstream — one edge recorded twice, in opposite directions. Add the edge to the UPSTREAM array of the dependent asset and re-run build.

dependencies.edge_kind_rule: ⚠️ EDGE KIND MATTERS AND fxUSD's HAND-WRITTEN DOWNSTREAM LIST CONFLATED TWO. `backing` means my SOLVENCY depends on this asset; `venue` means my EXIT PRICE does. Both are real and the response differs — a backing dependency moving calls for a re-read of the collateral analysis, a venue dependency moving calls for a re-read of the liquidity axis. A work queue that cannot tell them apart sends the same instruction for both.
